summary: The note describes how local political parties are using social media in the 2023 local election season to reach voters. It covers mobile-first content, video, data-driven targeting, localized content, influencers, real-time responsiveness, youth outreach, analytics, accessibility and emerging AI tools. It also warns about misinformation and stresses that direct, authentic communication remains the key to winning voters.
one_line: Local political parties in the 2023 election season rely on social media tactics like video, targeting, influencers and analytics, while guarding against misinformation.
key_facts: Donna White, a councilwoman running for reelection in November 2023, says social media is "about starting conversations, not just broadcasting messages."
A campaign manager for mayoral candidate Rajiv Consul says investing in mobile-friendly content is "not an option, it's a necessity."
A survey conducted in October 2023 by the Local Council Communication Group (LCCG) found that video posts saw a 56% higher engagement rate than text posts.
Sophia Rodriguez, mayor of Brookfield, regularly hosts live Q&A sessions on social media to bring down barriers between her office and the people.
Local party strategist Henry Talbot defends targeted advertising based on demographics, interests and behaviors: "Why speak into the void when you can talk directly to those who will listen?"
Election cycles in 2023 show a shift toward content on community identity and local issues, such as localized memes, infographics and short stories, rather than broad political rhetoric.
Local celebrities and influencers are used as endorsers to lend authenticity and reach voters disconnected from traditional political channels.
Incumbent council member Jesse Turner's campaign has specialized teams monitoring and responding to social media around the clock.
Parties target younger voters on TikTok and Snapchat with messages on climate change, employment opportunities and affordable housing.
Misinformation spreads quickly on social media, so parties must fact-check and establish themselves as credible sources.
Parties track engagement rates, reach and conversions to adjust strategy in real time.
Local parties add text transcripts, video captions and image descriptions so content is accessible to people with disabilities.
Predictive analytics, chatbots and AI-driven content creation are areas local parties are beginning to explore.
